Reference Table

Specific Heat Capacities (c)

Heat equation

q = m × c × ΔT
q = heat (J) · m = mass (g) · c = specific heat (J/g·°C) · ΔT = change in temperature (°C)

Change in temperature

ΔT = Tfinal − Tinitial
Positive ΔT means it warmed up. Negative ΔT means it cooled down.

Conservation of energy (calorimeter)

qlost = −qgained
The heat lost by the hot sample equals the heat gained by the water, with the opposite sign.

Solving for c

c = q ÷ (m × ΔT)

Food energy

1 Cal = 1 kcal = 1000 cal = 4184 J
Food “Calories” (capital C) are kilocalories.
Energy per gram = Calories ÷ grams burned
% difference = |measured − label| ÷ label × 100

Water

Density = 1.00 g/mL, so 1 mL of water has a mass of 1 g.
cwater = 4.184 J/g·°C
